doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Piano influences and the Hard Bop label
title: Is Cedar Walton a Romantic? Love of ballads and standards
summary: Brower suggests a romantic affection for standards; Walton does not know the term but admits he loves love songs and has heard hundreds of songs he recreates in his style.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Do you think of yourself as a, as a romantic?
In terms of maybe you're interested in developing melody and exploring all the implications of that?
Uh, I don't exactly know what that means, musically, romantic. You mean like uh, uh, Beethoven or Brahms or somebody in the jazz uh, were romantic? Who, who … I don't know what romantic is.
Well, I think I'm thinking about a bunch of things. I think I'm thinking about Romanticism in music …

And I'm also thinking about the affection for, for ballads, for standards and really bringing out the, the values, the musical values in those standards, which I find interesting, just … when you talked about composers, you talk about really … like Stravinsky …
…and things like that, and when I think of how you explore um, the standard repertoire …
… there seems to be an affection for these, for the qualities of these songs.

Yeah. Well, uh, perhaps I am a Romantic, but uh, for you asking me that, I wouldn't know whether to say yes or no. I, I really wouldn't. I uh, uh, If you …If you think I am, I am. That's the way I look at that. I don't know how to apply uh, someone being a Romantic to what I play, to, to, to, to how I play, how I … I certainly love uh, uh love songs, you know. I mean uh …
You just seem to have an inner sort of … with these, uh, inexhaustible access to songs.
You must know hundreds and hundreds of songs.

Well, may one hundred. [laughs] I would be surprised at hundreds and hundreds, but uh, uh I've heard hundreds and hundreds and uh, chosen to uh, uh, try to uh, uh, recreate them in my style in many instances.
